sections.content:
32,890 people

were counted on the census as "dental practitioners" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Dental practitioners diagnose dental and oral diseases, injuries and disorders, prescribe and administer treatment, recommend preventative action and, where necessary, refer the patient to a specialist.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "dental practitioners", 16.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "dental practitioners" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "dental practitioners" included:

  • solicitors and lawyers
  • sales accounts and business development managers
  • hairdressing and beauty salon managers and proprietors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "dental practitioners" there were a similar number of men and women (48% compared with 52%).

This means "dental practitioners" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 48% and women made up 52% of "dental practitioners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "dental practitioners" included:

  • other vocational and industrial trainers
  • textiles, garments and related trades (other)
  • packers, bottlers, canners and fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "dental practitioners", 3.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (68.5% compared with 31.5%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (75.9%) than an employee (24.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
